react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is overwhelmingly dominated by the arachidonic acid cascade, with five of seven inputs being eicosanoids and their direct precursors. Across three independent analytical paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (WikiPathways SMPDB), Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the consensus winner is arachidonic acid metabolism. In the RaMP ORA, Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) ranked first with an FDR of 6.84e-14 and a fold enrichment of 1430, driven by five input hits: 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, and arachidonic acid. The same five compounds appeared across all 14 next-ranked SMPDB drug-action pathways (NSAID action pathways) at FDR 1.79e-13, reflecting their shared positioning as COX and LOX substrates. Mummichog identified Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top m/z-active network (p = 5.88e-4, 11 of 11 compounds matched), with Leukotriene metabolism (rank 3, p = 0.034) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (rank 4, p = 0.048) as corroborating subnetworks. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) with the same four eicosanoid hits. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the shared substrate at the apex of all three branches: 5-lipoxygenase generates 5-HETE and leukotriene A4, 15-lipoxygenase generates 15-HETE, and cyclooxygenase generates 15-deoxy-PGJ2. The biological story is one of coordinated eicosanoid axis activation, consistent with an inflammatory, COX/LOX-inducing, or PPAR-gamma-activating treatment perturbation. Glycolaldehyde (glycerophospholipid branch) and Losartan (AT1 receptor antagonist, intersecting renin-angiotensin-eicosanoid cross-talk) represent secondary or modulatory signals.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differentially abundant metabolite set is overwhelmingly dominated by the arachidonic acid cascade, with five of seven inputs being eicosanoids and their direct precursors. Across three independent analytical paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA (WikiPathways SMPDB), Mummichog m/z-direct network analysis, and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the consensus winner is arachidonic acid metabolism. In the RaMP ORA, Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) ranked first with an FDR of 6.84e-14 and a fold enrichment of 1430, driven by five input hits: 5(S)-HETE, 15(S)-HETE, leukotriene A4, 15-deoxy-delta-12,14-prostaglandin J2, and arachidonic acid. The same five compounds appeared across all 14 next-ranked SMPDB drug-action pathways (NSAID action pathways) at FDR 1.79e-13, reflecting their shared positioning as COX and LOX substrates. Mummichog identified Arachidonic acid metabolism as the top m/z-active network (p = 5.88e-4, 11 of 11 compounds matched), with Leukotriene metabolism (rank 3, p = 0.034) and Prostaglandin formation from arachidonate (rank 4, p = 0.048) as corroborating subnetworks. MetaboAnalystR PSEA confirmed KEGG:hsa00590 (Arachidonic acid metabolism) with the same four eicosanoid hits. Arachidonic acid (KEGG:C00219) is the shared substrate at the apex of all three branches: 5-lipoxygenase generates 5-HETE and leukotriene A4, 15-lipoxygenase generates 15-HETE, and cyclooxygenase generates 15-deoxy-PGJ2. The biological story is one of coordinated eicosanoid axis activation, consistent with an inflammatory, COX/LOX-inducing, or PPAR-gamma-activating treatment perturbation. Glycolaldehyde (glycerophospholipid branch) and Losartan (AT1 receptor antagonist, intersecting renin-angiotensin-eicosanoid cross-talk) represent secondary or modulatory signals.
